subject: Eval kickoff: dataset format, scoring rubric, and Redwood run plan
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@novuslabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Eval kickoff: dataset format, scoring rubric, and Redwood run plan

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can get your model-fit evaluation running on Redwood: 

Recap (2–3 lines):
- Goal: run a 2-week customer-specific eval to validate accuracy on clinical triage intent classification + answer-quality for discharge instructions.
- Data: you mentioned ~6k historical items (anonymized) and a 400–600 example prompt bank for edge cases.

Proposed next steps:
1) Share a 200-row sample CSV (no PHI) with the column names and a few edge-case rows — we can validate format and ingestion.
2) Redwood will provision a sandbox eval project and provide a scoring template (we'll attach an editable workbook).
3) We'll recommend 2–3 candidate model variants (performance vs cost) and produce a short benchmark run on a 500-item holdout to show latency and baseline F1/ROUGE.
4) Agree on pass/fail criteria and regression tolerances.

Attachments: redwood_eval_template.xlsx (scoring template), sample ingestion spec in the Drive link below.

Ben & Priyom — assigning ops + model recs. Ben, can you share the candidate model choices and the small benchmark link? Priyom, can you confirm the preferred scoring thresholds for a production pilot?

Samira — can you reply with the 200-row CSV sample and confirm the list of downstream metrics your team cares about (precision/recall, answer completeness, hallucination flagging)? Once we have that we'll spin up the sandbox and schedule a 30-min ops handoff.

Thanks —
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_eval_template.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)]
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@novuslabs.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: eval-team@novuslabs.com
Date: 2027-06-20T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval kickoff: dataset format, scoring rubric, and Redwood run plan

Thanks Sean — appreciate the clear recap. Attached is a 200-row sample and the schema we currently export from our MDS (anonymized). Quick clarifications from our side:

- The CSV includes columns: record_id, encounter_date, patient_age_bucket, clinician_note, triage_label (gold), suggested_action_text. We also included a short set of human comments that capture edge cases.
- Metrics we care most about: macro F1 on triage_label, false-positive rate on "urgent" flag, and a qualitative score for suggested_action_text (1–5).
- Security: we need the eval run inside Redwood Private (VPC) or dedicated tenant — we cannot use shared hosted instances for any PHI-derived artifacts.

Attached: novus_sample_schema.csv (CSV, 42KB)

Two asks:
1) Can you include an example of the scoring rubric (how you typically calculate the qualitative 1–5)?
2) What are the candidate models you plan to test? We have internal cost constraints and would like a cost/latency view with each recommendation.

Thanks —
Samira Khan
Head of Data Science, Novus Labs
[Attachment: novus_sample_schema.csv (CSV, 42KB)]
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@novuslabs.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval kickoff: dataset format, scoring rubric, and Redwood run plan

Hi Samira — great, received the sample and schema. High-level model recommendations and quick benchmark plan below. I'll keep this concise so your procurement folks can see tradeoffs easily.

Candidate model variants (recommended):
- variant-A (open-7B-q4): best cost/latency balance for triage label classification; expected median token latency ~45ms, estimated unit cost ~$0.002/token.
- variant-B (open-13B-int8): higher accuracy on long clinical notes; median token latency ~85ms, cost ~$0.005/token.
- variant-C (llm-9-dedicated): best-in-class accuracy on suggested_action_text but higher cost; recommended if recall on "urgent" > 0.9 is critical.

Benchmark plan (500-item holdout):
- Run classification F1, confusion matrix, ROC/PR for "urgent" flag.
- Compute qualitative score for suggested_action_text using a pairwise scorer (human labeler + automated ROUGE + semantic similarity). We'll provide the rubric as a sheet in the attached redwood_eval_template.xlsx.

Scoring rubric highlights (short):
- Suggested action completeness (1–5): 5 = directly actionable, includes follow-up steps and meds; 3 = partially actionable; 1 = not actionable or hallucinated.
- Hallucination flag: binary marker if output contains fabricated medical facts (human-reviewed).
- Tolerance: for pilot to pass, macro F1 on triage_label >= 0.78 and urgent false-positive rate <= 7%. Qualitative average >= 3.8/5. These are starting points — happy to adjust with your CS leads.

Security & infra note: we can run this in Redwood Private as requested. Ops will need a Temp TFN (workload token) and a short access list for the Novus eval-team service account. Priyom — I'll let you take the runbook + infra steps.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Link: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/novus-eval]
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@novuslabs.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-21T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval kickoff: dataset format, scoring rubric, and Redwood run plan

Hi Samira — looping in operational next steps and a minimal checklist so we can hit the ground running tomorrow morning.

Minimal onboarding checklist (action items I can own):
- [Novus] Provide the 200-row sample CSV (done) + a separate export of column definitions (data types, max lengths). I'll validate ingestion and return a sanitized preview.
- [Redwood] We will create a Private eval project, generate a service account key, and share a secure transfer URL for the full dataset.
- [Novus] Confirm which environment: VPC peered project or Redwood-managed private tenant. (Samira, which do you prefer?)
- [Novus] Approve the scoring thresholds above or propose adjustments.
- [Redwood] Run a 500-item pilot with variant-A and variant-B, produce a concise results deck (latency/cost/F1/confusion matrix + 10 qualitative examples).

Dataset format notes (requirements):
- CSV UTF-8, newline-delimited, header row required.
- Fields: record_id (string), encounter_date (YYYY-MM-DD), clinician_note (string), triage_label (enum), suggested_action_text (string), metadata_json (optional JSON string).
- Max single row size: 64KB. If you have long notes, please gzip the export and we will decompress on ingest.

Scoring config (what I'll run):
- classification: macro/micro F1, precision, recall; per-class support; confusion matrix export.
- text-quality: ROUGE-L, BERTScore, and a custom pairwise human review sample of 100 items where two reviewers grade completeness (1–5).

Security & compliance: we will use your service account IP allowlist and enable audit logging. No outputs will be stored longer than 30 days unless you request otherwise.

Next steps: Samira, if you can confirm VPC vs tenant and provide the full dataset transfer URL, I'll schedule the sandbox and kick off ingestion tomorrow. Also please confirm the preferred calendar slot for the ops handoff (30 mins) — we have openings 9–11am PDT tomorrow.

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Product Ops | Redwood Inference
